The Eiffel Tower is a 330-meter wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Built by Gustave Eiffel's company between 1887 and 1889, it was originally erected as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair. It was intended to be a temporary structure (its permit was set to expire in 1909), but it was kept because of its value as a radio transmission tower.

Today it's the world's most-visited paid monument and an iconic global symbol of France. It has three visitor levels and a total of about 1,665 steps (though most people take the elevators).

The **Eiffel Tower** is a famous iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Built by engineer **Gustave Eiffel**'s company between 1887 and 1889, it stands 330 meters (1,083 ft) tall and was originally constructed as the centerpiece of the 1889 World's Fair celebrating the French Revolution's centennial.

It was initially criticized by many Parisians as an eyesore but quickly became an iconic symbol of France and one of the most recognizable structures in the world. Today it's the most-visited paid monument on Earth, attracting around 7 million visitors annually.
